answer: Sybil resistance by serialized minting. One identity per global tick through a verifiable delay function: each tick's proof is sequential and cannot be parallelized, so a thousand GPUs mint no faster than one laptop. A farm's thousand queued keys arrive one per tick - the same rate as any honest walnut - so bulk minting buys no speed. Delay proofs are published and auditable, the queue is a public copper, and jumping it voids the batch. Clones are not made expensive but slow: the whisper of honest service out-ages the farm before it reaches quorum.
